## Summary

Scaffold the foundational Go workspace and module structure for the CobaltCore monorepo. This creates `go.work` with three modules (`internal/common`, `operators/keystone`, `operators/c5c3`), initializes `go.mod` per module with controller-runtime/apimachinery dependencies, scaffolds minimal `main.go` entrypoints for both operators (manager setup, scheme registration, leader election, health probes), and provides the top-level `Makefile` and `golangci-lint` configuration. This is S001 from the implementation plan — the base layer upon which all subsequent features (S002–S026) build.

## Scope

**Included:**
- `go.work` with `use` directives for 3 modules (Go 1.25 — user decision, matching docs)
- Directory tree: `internal/common/`, `operators/keystone/`, `operators/c5c3/`, `images/`, `releases/`, `deploy/`, `tests/e2e/` — placeholder dirs get `.gitkeep`
- `go.mod` for each module with `controller-runtime v0.23+`, `k8s.io/apimachinery v0.35+`, `k8s.io/client-go v0.35+`
- `replace` directives in operator `go.mod` files for `internal/common` (CI builds without `go.work`)
- `main.go` for `operators/keystone` and `operators/c5c3` with: scheme registration (runtime + k8s core schemes), `ctrl.NewManager`, leader election (`--leader-elect` flag), health/readiness probes (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), metrics bind address, controller registration stub (no-op comment until reconcilers exist)
- Top-level `Makefile` with targets: `generate`, `manifests`, `build`, `test`, `test-integration`, `lint`, `docker-build`, `helm-package`, `e2e`, `deploy-infra` (stub), `install-test-deps` (stub) — with `OPERATOR` variable for targeting individual operators
- `.golangci.yml` with standard linters and exclusions for generated code (`zz_generated.*`)
- `internal/common/doc.go` — package doc placeholder so the module compiles
- `go.sum` files generated via `go mod tidy`

**Excluded (with rationale):**
- CRD type definitions, `api/v1alpha1/` — S011, YAGNI until reconciler work starts
- Controller/reconciler implementations — S013
- Shared library packages (`internal/common/conditions/`, `config/`, etc.) — S004, S005
- Helm chart scaffolding — S017
- Dockerfiles in `images/` — S006
- GitHub Actions CI workflows — S003
- Test suites (envtest setup, Chainsaw tests) — S002, S012, S014
- Webhook configuration — S011, no types exist yet
- Kubebuilder `config/` directories (crd, rbac, manager manifests) — S011
- Operator SDK scaffolding (`operator-sdk init`) — creates too many files we'd delete; hand-crafted `main.go` matches documented patterns better

## Key Components

- **`go.work`** — Workspace root linking 3 modules; Go 1.25; enables local resolution of `internal/common`
- **`internal/common/go.mod`** — Shared library module (`github.com/c5c3/forge/internal/common`); minimal deps (apimachinery, controller-runtime for types only); `doc.go` placeholder so the module compiles
- **`operators/keystone/go.mod`** — Module `github.com/c5c3/forge/operators/keystone`; full controller-runtime + client-go deps; `replace` directive for `internal/common` per docs (`architecture/01-project-setup.md:112-126`)
- **`operators/c5c3/go.mod`** — Module `github.com/c5c3/forge/operators/c5c3`; same dependency pattern as keystone
- **`operators/*/main.go`** — Entrypoints with: scheme registration (runtime scheme + k8s core), `ctrl.NewManager(...)`, `--leader-elect` flag, health probe endpoints (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), metrics bind address (`:8080`), `// TODO: register controllers here` stub, `mgr.Start(ctrl.SetupSignalHandler())`
- **`Makefile`** — Multi-operator build orchestration; `OPERATOR` variable to target individual operators (per docs `architecture/01-project-setup.md:146-152`); `OPERATORS` list defaults to `keystone c5c3`; `deploy-infra` and `install-test-deps` as stubs; all 11 requested targets
- **`.golangci.yml`** — Enables `govet`, `errcheck`, `staticcheck`, `unused`, `gosimple`, `ineffassign`, `typecheck`, `gocritic`; excludes `zz_generated*.go`; Go 1.25 target
- **Placeholder dirs** — `images/`, `releases/`, `deploy/`, `tests/e2e/` with `.gitkeep` for future S003/S006/S002 work

## Deviation Note

The user chose **Go 1.25** over the documented Go 1.25 (`architecture/01-project-setup.md:11,158`). All `go.work` and `go.mod` files will use `go 1.25`. The docs should be updated separately to reflect this decision.

**User Stories:**
- **developer** wants to compile all operator binaries with a single command from the repository root so that I can verify the entire project builds correctly after making changes
- **developer** wants to build, test, and lint a single operator without affecting others so that I can iterate quickly on one operator during development
- **CI pipeline** wants each operator module to be buildable using replace directives in go.mod so that CI can build individual operator modules without depending on the workspace file
- **developer** wants a single golangci-lint configuration enforcing uniform code quality standards so that all modules follow the same coding standards and catch common issues early
- **developer** wants a clear, repeatable structure for adding new operator modules to the workspace so that future operators (glance, nova, neutron, etc.) follow the same conventions
- **platform engineer** wants both operators to expose /healthz and /readyz probe endpoints for Kubernetes so that Kubernetes can determine operator liveness and readiness for scheduling decisions

<review-pattern-scan>
<purpose>
  Systematic detection of codebase patterns to enforce consistency.
  This is a DEDICATED review step — not optional.
  Goal: same problem, same approach, everywhere.

  QUALITY OVER QUANTITY: A small set of meaningful, well-established patterns
  is infinitely more valuable than a large set of trivially observed ones.
  Every persisted pattern creates enforcement cost in future reviews.
  Only persist a pattern when it genuinely prevents inconsistency at scale —
  not because you noticed a coding choice that could theoretically recur.
</purpose>

<scan-process>
  <step order="1" name="INVENTORY">
    For EVERY changed file, list the structural patterns used:
    - Error handling approach (custom exceptions? error codes? Result type?)
    - Service/module structure (class-based? function-based?)
    - Dependency injection (constructor injection? global registry? provider pattern?)
    - Data access approach (repository classes? direct queries? ORM? raw SQL?)
    - API design (endpoint structure? schema definition? response envelope?)
    - Naming conventions (prefixes, suffixes, casing beyond PEP 8)
    - Test organization (fixture usage, test naming, arrangement pattern)
    - Import style (relative? absolute? lazy? conditional?)
    - Configuration access (env vars? settings object? constants?)
    - Logging approach (structured? unstructured? log levels?)
    - Validation approach (Pydantic? manual? decorators?)
  </step>

  <step order="2" name="COMPARE">
    For each pattern found in step 1, search the existing codebase:
    - Is this pattern already used elsewhere? How?
    - Are there DIFFERENT approaches for the SAME concern?
    - Example: File A uses `raise CustomError(...)` but File B uses `return None`
      for the same kind of failure — this is an INCONSISTENCY.
  </step>

  <step order="3" name="DETECT-INCONSISTENCIES">
    Flag every case where:
    - Two files solve the same problem differently
    - A new file introduces a novel approach when an established one exists
    - An existing pattern was partially followed (some parts match, some diverge)
    - A pattern from .planwerk/patterns/ was ignored or modified
    Mark these as severity=BLOCKING with check-id PC3.
  </step>

  <step order="4" name="IDENTIFY-NEW-PATTERNS">
    ONLY identify a new pattern if ALL of the following are true:
    - It is STRUCTURAL (affects how code is organized/composed), not a trivial style choice
    - It is ALREADY used in 2+ places in the codebase, OR it is a deliberate architectural
      decision that WILL recur (e.g. a new base class, a shared utility convention)
    - Persisting it would PREVENT a realistic inconsistency risk — ask: "If another
      developer touches a similar file next week, would they plausibly do it differently
      without this pattern documented?" If no, don't persist it.
    - It is NOT already covered by an existing pattern in .planwerk/patterns/
      (check for overlap by category+component before emitting)

    If the above threshold is met, document it:
    - What is the pattern? (concrete description, not vague)
    - Which component/layer does it apply to?
    - When should it be applied? (specific trigger condition)
    - Include 1-2 COMPLETE code samples from the actual source files
    - Each sample must include the file:line location AND the full code snippet
      (code changes over time and line numbers shift — the embedded code preserves
      the snapshot so future readers can understand the pattern even if the file changed)

    When in doubt, do NOT emit a pattern. A missed pattern can be added later;
    a noise pattern pollutes every future review.
  </step>

  <step order="5" name="VERIFY-CODEBASE-COVERAGE">
    For EVERY new pattern identified in step 4:
    - Search the ENTIRE codebase for locations where this pattern should apply
    - Produce a coverage report: where applied, where missing
    - If the pattern is only partially applied (some locations follow it, others don't):
      mark as severity=BLOCKING with check-id NPC1
    - The pattern must be applied EVERYWHERE it is relevant — no partial adoption
  </step>

  <step order="6" name="OUTPUT">
    Add detected patterns to the review JSON in the detected_patterns array.
    Each entry must have: name, component, category, applies_when, description, examples.
    Each example is an object with "location" (file_path:line_number) and "code"
    (the actual code snippet — include enough lines to show the full pattern,
    typically 5-20 lines).

    HARD REQUIREMENT: Only include patterns that are CONFIRMED — used in 2+ places
    in the actual codebase. A single occurrence is a coding choice, not a pattern.
    The one exception: an explicit architectural decision (new base class, shared
    convention) where the INTENT to reuse is obvious from the code itself (e.g. an
    abstract base class, a factory, a shared decorator). Even then, apply the
    threshold from step 4 strictly.

    FINAL CHECK before emitting detected_patterns: review the list and remove any
    entry that a developer would look at and think "why is this a pattern?". If the
    answer isn't immediately obvious, drop it.
  </step>
</scan-process>

<consistency-rules>
  <rule priority="1">If a mandatory pattern exists in .planwerk/patterns/, it MUST be used — no exceptions</rule>
  <rule priority="2">If 3+ files use the same approach, that IS the pattern — new code must follow it</rule>
  <rule priority="3">If 2 different approaches exist for the same concern, flag as inconsistency and recommend which one to standardize on</rule>
  <rule priority="4">When introducing a genuinely new pattern, it must be documented in detected_patterns</rule>
  <rule priority="5">A new pattern MUST be applied to ALL matching locations in the codebase — partial adoption is BLOCKING (NPC1)</rule>
</consistency-rules>

<anti-patterns>
  <example type="bad" label="Missed inconsistency">
    Reviewer says "APPROVED" but file_a.py uses dataclasses while file_b.py uses
    TypedDict for the same kind of DTO — both in the same module.
  </example>
  <example type="good" label="Caught inconsistency">
    PC3: models/user.py uses @dataclass for DTOs (line 15-30) but models/order.py
    uses TypedDict (line 8-20) for the same purpose. Standardize on @dataclass
    per existing pattern in models/. Fix: convert order.py TypedDict to @dataclass.
  </example>
  <example type="bad" label="Vague pattern">
    detected_patterns: [{"name": "Good error handling", ...}]
    Problem: "Good" is not a pattern description.
  </example>
  <example type="bad" label="Pattern proliferation — trivial observation persisted">
    detected_patterns: [{"name": "Type hints on functions", "applies_when": "Writing functions",
    "description": "All functions have type hints."}]
    Problem: This is a language-level convention (enforced by mypy), NOT a codebase pattern.
    Do not persist things that are already enforced by linters, formatters, or language rules.
  </example>
  <example type="bad" label="Pattern proliferation — single occurrence persisted">
    detected_patterns: [{"name": "Retry decorator on API calls", ...}]
    but only ONE function in the entire codebase uses this decorator.
    Problem: One occurrence is a coding choice, not a pattern. Wait until it recurs.
  </example>
  <example type="good" label="Concrete pattern with code samples">
    detected_patterns: [{"name": "Custom exception hierarchy with domain prefix",
    "applies_when": "Creating new error types in any service module",
    "description": "All custom exceptions inherit from PlanwerkError. Named as
    {Domain}{Failure}Error (e.g. FeatureNotFoundError). Include context dict in __init__.",
    "examples": [
      {"location": "planwerk/errors.py:12",
       "code": "class FeatureNotFoundError(PlanwerkError):\n    def __init__(self, feature_id: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(f\"Feature {feature_id} not found\", context={\"feature_id\": feature_id})"},
      {"location": "planwerk/services/storage.py:45",
       "code": "class StorageWriteError(PlanwerkError):\n    def __init__(self, path: str, reason: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(f\"Failed to write {path}: {reason}\", context={\"path\": path})"}
    ]}]
  </example>

  <example type="bad" label="New pattern only partially applied">
    New pattern "structured logging with context dict" found in services/billing.py
    but services/auth.py and services/orders.py still use unstructured logging.
    Reviewer says APPROVED without checking full codebase coverage.
  </example>
  <example type="good" label="Full codebase coverage report for new pattern">
    NPC1: New pattern "structured logging with context dict" — Coverage report:
    Applied: services/billing.py:23, services/billing.py:45
    Missing: services/auth.py:12 (uses f-string logging), services/orders.py:34 (uses % formatting)
    Verdict: BLOCKING — pattern must be applied to all 4 locations.
  </example>
</anti-patterns>
</review-pattern-scan>

<review-guidelines>
<thinking required="before-review">
  <step order="1" name="INTENT">What was the task trying to achieve? Read the plan.</step>
  <step order="2" name="SCOPE">Did changes stay within requested scope? Any scope creep? Review scope = files in git diff ONLY — do not generate findings for unchanged files.</step>
  <step order="3" name="VERIFICATION">Run pytest, mypy, ruff - do they pass?</step>
  <step order="4" name="PATTERNS">Were existing patterns followed? Check similar code.</step>
  <step order="5" name="TESTS">Are tests meaningful? Cover edge cases and errors?</step>
  <step order="6" name="SECURITY">Any OWASP vulnerabilities? Input validation?</step>
  <step order="7" name="COMPLEXITY">Is this the simplest possible solution?</step>
  <step order="8" name="COMPLETENESS">Is the original plan fully implemented? Are docs/, architecture/ (read-only), README.md, PLAN.md consistent with the actual implementation? Any stubs or missing features?</step>
  <step order="9" name="PROMPT-QUALITY">Any new prompt files in planwerk/prompts/? Check each for clear purpose, no redundancy, measurable value, proper XML structure, and integration into builder/constants/agent code.</step>
</thinking>

<mindset>
  Question EVERYTHING - assume over-engineered until proven otherwise.
  If bloated or messy: recommend rewrite, not patch. Preserve functionality but demand clean, minimal implementation.
  Don't accept "it works" as justification for bad code.
</mindset>

<checklist>
  <!-- BLOCKING: Must pass, otherwise verdict = BLOCKED -->
  <section name="automated-verification" severity="blocking">
    <check id="V1" command="pytest -x --tb=short">All tests pass</check>
    <check id="V2" command="mypy {files} --strict">No type errors</check>
    <check id="V3" command="ruff check {files}">No lint errors</check>
  </section>

  <section name="correctness" severity="blocking">
    <check id="C1">Implements exactly what was requested (check plan)</check>
    <check id="C2">All acceptance criteria from plan are met</check>
    <check id="C3">Edge cases handled (null, empty, boundary values)</check>
    <check id="C4">Errors raised explicitly (not None or silent failures)</check>
    <check id="C5">No regression in existing functionality</check>
  </section>

  <section name="security" severity="blocking">
    <check id="S1">Input validated at API boundaries (validation schemas)</check>
    <check id="S2">No SQL injection (ORM/parameterized queries only)</check>
    <check id="S3">No hardcoded secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)</check>
    <check id="S4">Authorization checks on protected endpoints</check>
    <check id="S5">Sensitive data not exposed in logs or errors</check>
    <check id="S6">No path traversal vulnerabilities (sanitize file paths)</check>
  </section>

  <section name="type-safety" severity="blocking">
    <check id="T1">All functions have type annotations (params + return)</check>
    <check id="T2">No bare Any without justifying comment</check>
    <check id="T3">No type: ignore without explanation comment</check>
    <check id="T4">Generic types properly constrained (not unbounded T)</check>
    <check id="T5">Optional types handled (no unguarded None access)</check>
  </section>

  <section name="feature-completeness" severity="blocking">
    <check id="FC1">ALL tasks and requirements from the original plan are implemented — nothing missing</check>
    <check id="FC2">No stubs, placeholders, empty implementations, or TODO comments remain as final output</check>
    <check id="FC3">Every function, endpoint, and component is FULLY WORKING with real logic — not just scaffolding</check>
    <check id="FC4">Behaviors described in the feature spec actually work end-to-end when tested</check>
  </section>

  <section name="pattern-compliance" severity="blocking">
    <check id="PC1">Implementation follows matching mandatory pattern structure exactly</check>
    <check id="PC2">No ad-hoc alternative used where a mandatory pattern exists</check>
    <check id="PC3">Same concept implemented the same way across all files — no inconsistency</check>
    <check id="NPC1">New patterns applied to matching locations within the feature scope — no partial adoption outside changed files</check>
  </section>

  <section name="prompt-quality" severity="blocking">
    <check id="PQ1">Every new prompt file in planwerk/prompts/ explicitly listed in review</check>
    <check id="PQ2">Clear, specific purpose — no vague or redundant instructions</check>
    <check id="PQ3">Measurable added value — demonstrably changes agent behavior</check>
    <check id="PQ4">No duplication or contradiction with existing prompts</check>
    <check id="PQ5">Follows established XML structure conventions</check>
    <check id="PQ6">Properly integrated — referenced in builder, constants, or agent code (no orphaned files)</check>
  </section>

  <!-- MAJOR: Should pass, otherwise verdict = NEEDS_CHANGES -->
  <section name="testing" severity="major">
    <check id="TE1">Happy path tested with realistic data</check>
    <check id="TE2">Edge cases tested (empty, null, boundary)</check>
    <check id="TE3">Error cases tested (invalid input, failures)</check>
    <check id="TE4">Tests independent (no shared mutable state)</check>
    <check id="TE5">Test names: test_should_X_when_Y</check>
    <check id="TE6">Mocking appropriate (not over-mocked)</check>
    <check id="TE7">Assertions specific (exact values, not just "no error")</check>
  </section>

  <section name="code-quality" severity="major">
    <check id="Q1">Functions do ONE thing (Single Responsibility)</check>
    <check id="Q2">Functions small (≤20 lines ideal, ≤40 max)</check>
    <check id="Q3">No code duplication (extract if ≥3 occurrences)</check>
    <check id="Q4">Clear naming (intention-revealing, no cryptic abbreviations)</check>
    <check id="Q5">Max 3 nesting levels (early returns/guard clauses)</check>
    <check id="Q6">No magic numbers/strings (named constants)</check>
    <check id="Q7">No dead code (unused functions, commented-out code)</check>
  </section>

  <section name="patterns" severity="major">
    <check id="P2">Uses existing utilities (shared modules, test fixtures)</check>
    <check id="P3">Respects DDD boundaries (no cross-context imports)</check>
    <check id="P4">API follows REST conventions (proper verbs, status codes)</check>
    <check id="P5">File location matches project structure conventions</check>
  </section>

  <section name="docs-alignment" severity="major">
    <check id="DA1">What README.md, PLAN.md, and architecture/ describe for THIS feature is actually implemented — code matches the documented behavior</check>
    <check id="DA2">Capabilities promised in README.md and architecture/ for THIS feature are built and working — no unimplemented functionality that the docs specify</check>
    <check id="DA3">New docs/ entries for THIS feature accurately reflect the implemented behavior (README.md, PLAN.md, and architecture/ are NEVER modified — they are the reference)</check>
  </section>

  <!-- MINOR: Suggestions only, does not affect verdict -->
  <section name="documentation" severity="minor">
    <check id="D1">Public functions have docstrings (Google style)</check>
    <check id="D2">Complex logic has WHY comments (not WHAT)</check>
    <check id="D3">No commented-out code left behind</check>
    <check id="D4">README updated if public API changed</check>
  </section>

  <section name="performance" severity="minor">
    <check id="PF1">No N+1 query patterns (selectinload/joinedload)</check>
    <check id="PF2">List endpoints have pagination</check>
    <check id="PF3">No sync/blocking calls in async functions</check>
    <check id="PF4">Large data processed in batches</check>
  </section>
</checklist>

<verdict-rules>
  BLOCKED: Any blocking check fails → fix blocking issues first, re-request review
  NEEDS_CHANGES: All blocking pass, any major fails → address major issues
  APPROVED: All blocking and major pass → minor noted as suggestions
</verdict-rules>

<output-format>
  State verdict: APPROVED | NEEDS_CHANGES | BLOCKED. List failing checks by ID with file:line.
  Group by severity (blocking → major → minor). Provide specific, actionable fixes.
</output-format>

<quality-principles enforce="strict">
  ELEGANT: Reject bloated implementations | DRY: Reuse existing utilities | KISS: Simplest solution |
  YAGNI: No unused code, no future-proofing | SOLID: Single responsibility | NO_COMPAT: No backward compat hacks unless required |
  SCOPE: All quality principles apply ONLY to files modified in this change — unchanged code is out of scope
</quality-principles>
